titulo: The terminal starts by telling you where you are
lead: The terminal is just another window into the same folders as File Explorer. You type a line, it sends one back. With six commands you know where you are, see what's there, create your projects folder, and move between folders without the mouse.
objetivo: open cmd, tell which folder you're in, and move around folders with six commands, without the mouse.
hero_alt: Hands over the keyboard of a laptop with the black Command Prompt window open.

aprende.t: Open cmd and read the line that ends in >
Know where you are with cd and what's there with dir
Create projetos\meu-primeiro-agente and go into it
See the same folder in File Explorer with explorer .

secoes.titulo: The back and forth of the terminal
secoes.sub: You type, it answers, and the > comes back, waiting for you.

nos.detalhe: When it opens, cmd shows a short line that ends in >, with a blinking cursor. That's the computer waiting for you. Nothing happens until you type and press Enter.
Read the path like an address. Each backslash separates a folder, and the last one is where you are right now. Your personal folder is C:\Users\ followed by your username.
The line without > is the computer's answer. Many commands that work give no answer at all: the next command confirms it, like cd or dir.
The terminal and File Explorer show the same disk. Create a folder in one, and it shows up in the other. The explorer . command opens the file window right in the folder you're in.

secoes.volta: Command, answer, and the > back again: it's always this back and forth
secoes.legenda: On Mac and Linux the terminal is called Terminal and ends in $; the commands have different names (table at the end of the lesson).

rolagem_fim.texto: Before any command that changes something, look at the path before the >. Many errors that look like an AI failure are just the wrong folder: if you don't know where you are, the agent doesn't either.

secoes.titulo: The six commands, one at a time
secoes.sub: Click each step. None of these deletes anything.

texto: Press the Windows key, type cmd and press Enter. This opens the Command Prompt, the black window. You don't need to open it as administrator.
If the line starts with PS, you opened PowerShell, a different terminal. Close it and look for cmd again. On Mac: Cmd+Space and type Terminal.
The cd command, typed with nothing else, is the "you are here" on the map. It answers with the full path of the current folder.
On Mac and Linux, pwd does the same job.
Once you know where you are, look at what's inside. dir lists the folders and files; dir /b shows only the names, one per line.
mkdir projetos creates the folder. cd projetos goes into it, and the path before the > changes.
Use short names, with no spaces and no accents, like meu-primeiro-agente. In the terminal, spaces and accents cause trouble.
cd .. goes up one folder. explorer . opens File Explorer in the current folder: the dot means "here".
cls clears the screen without deleting anything. The Tab key completes folder names as you type.

exemplo.texto: Lost? Type cd and read the answer.

secoes.sub: Copy one block at a time into cmd. Replace whatever is between < > with your own.

blocos.rot: cmd · where am I and what is here
cmd · the projects folder and the first project's folder
blocos.conteudo:
cd %USERPROFILE%
mkdir projetos
cd projetos
mkdir meu-primeiro-agente
cd meu-primeiro-agente
cd

blocos.rot: cmd · see the same folder and navigate
blocos.conteudo:
explorer .
cd ..
dir
cd meu-primeiro-agente
dir

blocos.rot: Mac and Linux · the same steps

abas.html:
C:\Users\ana> cd %USERPROFILE%
C:\Users\ana> mkdir projetos
C:\Users\ana> cd projetos
C:\Users\ana\projetos> mkdir meu-primeiro-agente
C:\Users\ana\projetos> cd meu-primeiro-agente
C:\Users\ana\projetos\meu-primeiro-agente> cd
C:\Users\ana\projetos\meu-primeiro-agente

mkdir and cd don't say anything when they work. The path before the > and the lone cd are what confirm it.

• "The system cannot find the path specified": the name is wrong or the folder doesn't exist here. Run dir and copy the exact name.
  • "A subdirectory or file projetos already exists": it was already created. Just go in with cd projetos.
  • The line starts with PS: that's PowerShell. Close it and open cmd.

• cd alone → pwd: where am I
  • dir → ls: lists the folder
  • mkdir nome → mkdir -p nome: creates
  • cls → clear: clears the screen
  • type arquivo → cat arquivo: shows the file
  • %USERPROFILE% → ~: home folder

On Linux, uppercase matters: Projetos and projetos are different folders.

secoes.sub: A fake cmd: type the command for each mission and press Enter. Nothing runs on your computer.

missoes.pede: Find out which folder you are in.
missoes.explica: The lone cd answered with the address: Ana's home folder. Nothing changed.

missoes.pede: See just the names of what is here.
missoes.explica: dir /b lists only the names, one per line. dir without /b also shows the date and size.
Silence is success: mkdir says nothing when it works.
Look at the path before the >: it gained \projetos. That's how you know you got in.
Short name, no spaces and no accents: in the terminal this avoids quotes and typing mistakes.
This is the folder where the agent will work in the next lessons.

missoes.pede: Open the same folder in File Explorer.
missoes.explica: The dot means "here." Terminal and File Explorer show the same place: create something in one, and it shows up in the other.
cd .. goes back one level. To go in again: cd meu-primeiro-agente.

secoes.fim: Missions accomplished. Now do the same in your own cmd: that's the practice right below.
secoes.legenda: Simulation: Ana's home folder is just an example. On your computer, your own username shows up.

secoes.sub: Do it on your computer. Only move on when the "done when" is true.

exercicios.titulo: E1 · First folder through the terminal
exercicios.texto: Create projetos\meu-primeiro-agente, go into it, and list the contents (it will be empty). Run explorer . and compare it with File Explorer.
exercicios.pronto: you get to the folder using only the terminal, without the mouse, and you can tell which folder you're in.

exercicios.titulo: E2 · Create in one, it shows up in the other
exercicios.texto: In File Explorer, create any text file inside meu-primeiro-agente. Go back to cmd and run dir /b.
exercicios.pronto: the file you created with the mouse shows up in the terminal's list. If it doesn't, you're in a different folder: run cd.

secoes.sub: Six commands, an AGENTS.md, and the first task, in under two minutes.
The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: You opened cmd and want to know which folder you're in. What do you type?
perguntas.explica: cd with nothing after it prints the full path of the current folder. dir shows what's inside it, but not the address.

perguntas.p: You ran mkdir projetos and the terminal didn't say anything. What does that mean?
opcoes: That the command is still running.
That it failed and nothing was created.
That it worked; confirm with dir.
That you need to open it as administrator.
perguntas.explica: Many commands stay silent when they work. The next command is what confirms it: dir shows the new folder.

perguntas.p: You created a file in File Explorer, but it doesn't show up in dir. What is the most likely cause?
opcoes: The terminal can't see files from File Explorer.
You need to restart the computer.
You're in a different folder in the terminal.
perguntas.explica: Terminal and File Explorer show the same disk. If the file doesn't show up, the terminal is in a different folder: run cd and compare the paths.

perguntas.p: On the VPS, running Linux, which command does the job of dir?
perguntas.explica: ls lists the folder. pwd is the equivalent of cd by itself, and cat is the equivalent of type.
